solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Instant support

definitions.meaning: a very brief moment, as in 'wait a moment'
to back a motion or a candidate formally

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a tiny unit of time, and the verb for backing a proposal after it is moved.

clue.text: Footballers who demand better pay?

definitions.meaning: forwards whose job is to score goals
workers who down tools in a pay dispute

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one picture of greedy players, but it splits into two meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Goal-scoring forwards share a name with workers taking industrial action, and the question mark flags the pun.

clue.text: Old city transport outside hotel

indicators.note: the transport word sits outside, wrapping round the hotel letter

parts.note: cartage is the carrying of goods by cart
H is Hotel in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A tourist arranges a ride from outside their hotel to see an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Phoenician city in North Africa destroyed by Rome is a classic example of an old city.

clue.text: Useless Greek character, bad one being thrown out

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the numeral for one is ejected from the word for bad

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A worthless Greek, a bad sort, is expelled from somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Something void, having no force or value, is useless, as in a contract declared void.

clue.text: Sold with difficulty, a strange historical site

indicators.note: the letters of the word are forced awkwardly into a new order

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Something was sold only with difficulty, a strange historical site perhaps being a hard sell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with difficulty' rearranges SOLD to OLDS. OLD SARUM is the abandoned hill fort near Salisbury in England, famous as a 'rotten borough'.
explanation.definitionFit: The deserted earlier settlement of Salisbury, with Iron Age ramparts and cathedral ruins, is a well-known historical site.

clue.text: Space in literature given to frivolous No.1 celebrity

parts.note: leading is the typographer's term for space between printed lines, once made with strips of lead
light means trivial, as in light reading

explanation.surface: A literature page devotes space to some frivolous piece about a top celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent, influential person at the top of a field is called this idiom, so it suits a top celebrity.

clue.text: Terrible threat lying within grass could be overwhelming

indicators.note: the shuffled word lies inside the word for grass

parts.note: to grass is slang for to inform on someone, to sing

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters are badly mangled

explanation.surface: A menacing threat hidden in the grass could be overwhelming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is not the lawn of the surface but British slang for informing on someone; 'Terrible' and 'lying within' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A devastating experience can be described as shattering, meaning crushing or overwhelming in its effect.

clue.text: Sound of regret when meeting obstacle? This fixture on vehicle will limit damage

definitions.text: This fixture on vehicle will limit damage

indicators.note: the word for regret is said aloud and spelt as the Australian animal

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a bar is a barrier or obstacle

explanation.surface: A driver groans in regret on hitting an obstacle, wishing a fitting had limited the damage.
explanation.walkthrough: A roo bar is a sturdy frame on the front of a vehicle, named for kangaroos in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The grille guard bolted to the front of a car protects it from collision damage, so it is a protective fixture.

clue.text: See supposedly creative female torture he-man cruelly

indicators.note: cruelly suggests the words are twisted and tortured into another order

explanation.surface: A woman with supposed creativity tortures a muscle man cruelly.
explanation.definitionFit: The personified force of the natural world is imagined as a woman who creates all living things.

clue.text: Customer finally goes to a bank on very few occasions

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A customer at last goes to a bank, which they hardly ever do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is a verb here (bank on), not the place the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something seldom means doing it on very few occasions, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Holy man's ram, we may deduce?

indicators.note: we may deduce tells the solver to work backwards from the holy man's title to the animal it implies

parts.note: the animal we arrive at when the second half of the title is read as an instruction to stir the first

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer works out that a holy man owns the ram.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as MAR ABOUT: ABOUT then works as an anagram signal on MAR, giving RAM. The question mark warns of this reverse reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim hermit or saint in North Africa, often revered for piety, is a holy man.

clue.text: President will offer no great deal, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy here is an imperative to imagine the letters in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A sceptic thinks the president will offer no great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sandinista leader has been the elected head of state of Nicaragua, so he is a president.

clue.text: Something black coming from Chancellor

definitions.meaning: Helmut, the German Chancellor who oversaw reunification

explanation.definitionFit: The black cosmetic used to line the eyes shares its name with the long-serving German head of government.

clue.text: Wise men, holy person and judge — together such may administer law

parts.note: the Magi are the wise men of the Nativity
ST is short for saint
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: Wise men, a saint and a judge band together to dispense justice.
explanation.definitionFit: A justice of the peace or local court official who hears minor cases is someone who administers the law.

clue.text: Cuckoo smart, aping birds

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cuckoo, smart at aping other birds, as it mimics their eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' looks like a bird in the scene, but it is the signal to rearrange SMART APING.
explanation.definitionFit: These grouse of mountain and Arctic regions, white in winter, are game birds.

clue.text: Footballers who are likely to vote Conservative?

definitions.meaning: attacking players who run along the right flank

definitions.text: who are likely to vote Conservative?

explanation.definitionFit: Flank attackers on one side of the pitch share a name with right-leaning voters, the question mark marking the pun.

clue.text: Two characters as one showing unusual art and guile

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters taking an uncommon arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone shows unusual art and guile by acting as two characters at once.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, a pair of letters joined into a single glyph, such as ae or fi, is called this.

clue.text: Most violent storm's beginning on top of mountain

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits above the second
beginning picks out the opening letter of the word

parts.note: Everest is the world's highest mountain

explanation.surface: A storm starts at the summit of a mountain, at its most violent.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of harsh or intense describes the most violent or extreme case.

clue.text: Fab man can start to export oil

parts.note: brill is British slang for brilliant, fab
Ian is a man's name
a tin is a can

indicators.note: start to takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A great fellow can start to export oil.
explanation.definitionFit: This perfumed hair oil was used to make men's hair glossy, so it is an oil.

clue.text: King and queen and others — see them in gardens

definitions.meaning: cards of the black suit with a pointed leaf symbol

explanation.definitionFit: The playing-card suit containing a king and queen shares its name with the gardener's digging tools.

clue.text: Goddess 'as old-fashioned vitality, not half!

parts.note: the archaic form hath, with its h dropped as 'as drops one

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: energy means vitality

explanation.surface: A goddess has old-fashioned vitality, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'As is has with a dropped h, so its old form hath becomes 'ATH. 'Not half' keeps the first three letters of ENERGY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of wisdom and war, patron of Athens, is commonly spelt this way too.

clue.text: Party I arranged includes cunning arrangement to favour men

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the other piece within them
arranged signals putting the letters in a new order

parts.note: arch means sly or knowing

explanation.surface: A party I organised has a sly plan to favour men.
explanation.definitionFit: A social system in which men hold power is a structure built to favour men.

clue.text: Something that may be enclosed keeps female free from danger

indicators.note: keeps is used in the sense of holding something in custody, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: an SAE, a stamped addressed envelope, is enclosed with a letter for the reply

explanation.surface: An enclosure holds a woman out of harm's way.
explanation.walkthrough: An SAE is the British stamped addressed envelope sent so that someone can reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Being secure and out of harm's way is the plain synonym for being free from danger.

clue.text: Controversial show creating shocks?

definitions.meaning: the 1960s rock musical notorious for nudity
a shock is a thick mass of what grows on the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'Creating' joins the two senses; 'shocks' pretends to describe the show's effect on audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: The scandalous hippie musical shares its name with what grows on the head, a shock of it being a thick mop.

clue.text: In performance English man or woman played records

indicators.note: the English person goes in the performance word

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance
Jay is a name given to either sex

explanation.surface: An English performer of either sex spun records during a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To work as a disc jockey, playing records, is the verb form of the spelt-out DJ.

clue.text: See 8
Dealer in small things is mad, sense abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A trader in small goods goes mad, all sense abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small things' is a playful way of describing seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of plant seeds deals in tiny items, hence a dealer in small things.

clue.text: Heraldic colour of particular gentleman

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is taken from within the following words

explanation.surface: A refined gentleman has a heraldic colour on his coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry the tincture silver is called argent, one of the standard heraldic colours.
